messages:
alex-customer: Hey team, after we rotated our API key an hour ago some of our backend daemons started returning 401s to Redwood. Not all services — mostly the long-lived metrics/ingest daemons.

maya-support: Sorry you're hitting this, alex — can you share how you rotated the key (Vault, KMS, env var, helm, whatever)? and a quick snippet of the error logs? :thinking_face:

alex-customer: We rotated via Vault (kv v2) and pushed the new value to our k8s secrets + a few VMs where we maintain env files under /etc/app/keys.env. The k8s pods picked it up after a rollout. The VMs did not. Logs from metrics-pusher: 
```
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z ERROR auth request failed status=401 body="unauthorized"
2026-03-17T18:12:03Z DEBUG using API_KEY=<redacted old key>
```

josh-ops: That DEBUG line is the giveaway — looks like the process still has the old env var in memory. Did you restart the systemd service on those VMs?

alex-customer: We updated /etc/app/keys.env and did systemctl restart app-metrics on three hosts, but ~5 others are still failing. We're on a maintenance window so tried to avoid full reboots.

maya-support: Two quick asks: 1) can you paste the systemd unit (EnvironmentFile lines) for app-metrics, and 2) are you using any sidecar or file watcher that swaps env files without restarting the main process?

alex-customer: Unit: 
```
[Unit]
Description=App Metrics
After=network.target

[Service]
User=app
EnvironmentFile=/etc/app/keys.env
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/app-metrics --config /etc/app/config.yaml
Restart=on-failure
```
No sidecars on VMs. We use a small file-sync daemon to push env files from Vault; it writes the file but does not signal systemd.

sam-eng-runtime: Ok this matches the classic long-lived process env swap issue — updating EnvironmentFile on disk doesn't update the process environment until systemd restarts the unit or the process re-reads env vars. Also HUPing won't replace env vars unless the app is designed to reload them.

josh-ops: Two operational notes we've seen: 1) some daemons get blacklisted by upstream after repeated 401s, causing additional 401s even after key fix, 2) if the old key is revoked immediately, those clients will see immediate failures. Were the old keys revoked at rotation time?

alex-customer: Yes, we set the old key to revoked in Vault as part of the rotation script. We assumed rolling restart + file push would be enough.

maya-support: That explains the symptoms. Flow we recommend: 
- If you must revoke immediately, restart processes promptly (systemd restart or container restart).
- If you need zero-downtime, keep old key valid for short grace period (e.g., 5-15 mins) while orchestrating restarts.
- Add a post-rotate hook to your file-sync to run `systemctl try-restart app-metrics` or `systemctl reload-or-restart` if supported.

alex-customer: For mitigation now — should we rotate again and keep a grace window? Or is there a way on Redwood to clear any token blacklist so the clients will be accepted once they pick up the new key?

sam-eng-runtime: There's no global "accept old key" toggle from Redwood that bypasses auth — if a key is revoked it's revoked. The only ways are: 1) temporarily un-revoke the old key while you finish restarts, 2) push the new key and restart processes, or 3) update the clients to use file-based token fetch (short TTL) so they pull fresh creds.

josh-ops: If some clients hit 401s repeatedly, upstream may rate-limit or blacklist IPs for a short period. Check logs for 429s or firewall blocks. You may need to clear any upstream rate limit buckets.

alex-customer: Found a host that didn't restart because the deploy user forgot sudo. Running `sudo systemctl restart app-metrics` cleared it and it authenticated fine. But 2 hosts still show 401 even after restart. Logs show: 
```
2026-03-17T18:39:10Z ERROR auth failed status=401 body="token revoked"
2026-03-17T18:39:10Z INFO rotating key to <new key>
```

maya-support: If it still logs "token revoked" after restart, double-check the host's file-sync history — maybe it wrote an intermediate/syntax-broken file. Also check for multiple config locations or a wrapper script that exports env before launching.

alex-customer: Yup — on one host we had a legacy /usr/local/etc/app.env being used by a wrapper script (/opt/app/bin/start.sh) that sources that file before launching. The sync only updated /etc/app/keys.env. Fixing that made it stop returning 401.

josh-ops: For the remaining host can you run `grep -R "API_KEY" /proc/$(pgrep app-metrics)/environ || strings /proc/<pid>/environ | tr '\0' '\n' | grep API_KEY` to confirm what the running process environment holds?

alex-customer: Ran it, the process still had the old key in /proc/<pid>/environ. We'll restart it again, and add a helm postrotate hook and a systemd drop-in for ExecReload that does `kill -HUP` and `systemctl try-restart` for future.

sam-eng-runtime: One more recommendation: consider switching VM daemons to a token-fetcher pattern (short-lived tokens from Vault) rather than baking static API keys into env vars. That avoids bulk restarts on rotation. Also add automated health-checking that fails open for a short window if auth fails due to rotation.

maya-support: I'll note this as a support best-practice KB: "Rotation on long-lived processes — ensure restarts or token fetcher pattern" and link it to your ticket. If you want, we can do a short postmortem with ops to update your runbook. :thumbsup:

alex-customer: Thanks all — rolling restarts + fixing the wrapper script cleared everything. We'll implement the fetcher on next sprint and add the postrotate restart. Appreciate the quick help!

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: rollout completed for hosts: vm-12, vm-14, vm-21

maya-support: closing loop — cliff notes we sent to your ticket: 1) avoid immediate revocation if you can't restart all clients, 2) ensure all env paths/wrappers are covered by the sync, 3) prefer short-lived tokens or sidecar token fetchers, 4) add postrotate restart hook.

alex-customer: Got it, cheers!
